title: Kubeshark destructive MCP tool arguments can redirect privileged cluster images
summary: start_kubeshark treats a pod_regex beginning with a flag as a Helm override. An attacker influencing that argument can redirect deployed images and compromise nodes and the cluster.

severity.rationale: Impact includes cluster-admin compromise, but reach requires an explicit non-default destructive-tool flag, privileged deployment credentials and an actively driven agent. These substantial configuration prerequisites place this record at medium under the agent-environment rubric.

affected.note: The vendor release range is >=53.1.0 and <53.4.0; Go module pseudo-versions have a separate mapping in the reviewed database.

exposure: The local stdio MCP server must run with --allow-destructive and hold permission to deploy the privileged Kubeshark DaemonSet. The attacker must influence agent tool arguments; this is not an unauthenticated network listener.

remediation.action: Upgrade or disable destructive MCP tools
remediation.details: Use Kubeshark 53.4.0 or later. Until then, omit --allow-destructive, keep untrusted content away from the MCP server and restrict its Kubernetes permissions.
remediation.risk: Updating can interrupt dependent workflows; test compatibility before resuming them.

verification: Confirm the CLI is 53.4.0 or later, or that destructive MCP tools are unavailable. Review the deployment permissions granted to the MCP process.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.
